text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Sailor, explorer and surgeon GEORGE BASS (Bass Strait), was born on this day in 1771. In 1803 he vanished into the Pacific aboard the good ship VENUS.
JOHN JAMES was born in 1841. He became the Lands Registrar and a Magistrate in Western Australia.
Scottish explorer HENRY FORBES was born on this day in 1851.
Russian playwright ANTON CHEKHOV was born in 1860.

Australian meat exporter Sir WILLIAM ANGLISS, whose wide use of the freezing process made major inroads into world markets, was born in 1865. Something of a workaholic, he was in his office every day, even at the age of 92.
Australian racing driver NINA JONES was born in 1882. She raced her CROSSLEY, and later an ALFA ROMEO, in open competition and won many speedway and driving championships in the 1920s.
British Cabinet Minister JOHN PROFUMO, who became caught-up in the "Profumo Affair" with CHRISTINE KEELER and a Russian naval attache, was born in 1915.
HAROLD PRINCE, the American stage producer and director of hits such as "WEST SIDE STORY" and "EVITA", was born in 1928.
American actor GENE HACKMAN was born in 1931.
English actress VANESSA REDGRAVE was born in 1937.

British rock performer PHIL COLLINS was born in 1951. The drummer/singer/songwriter/producer and actor answered an ad in 1970 for a job as a drummer with the band 'Genesis'. He'd already had a long career as a child with appearances on TV, radio, film and on stage. In addition to playing with 'Genesis' COLLINS also performed with his own group 'Brand X' and in 1981 embarked on a solo career. His hits included "In The Air Tonight" (1981 and again in 1988), "You Can't Hurry Love" (1982), "Against All Odds" (1984), "Sussudio" (1985), "One More Night" (1985), "A Groovy Kind Of Love" (1988), "Two Hearts" (1988) and "Another Day in Paradise" (1989). He also had the
title role in the movie "Buster" in 1988. He also appears on several other artists' records as a studio musician.
** EVENTS **
1649 : King CHARLES I was beheaded in London for treason.
1835 : President ANDREW JACKSON survived the first ever
assassination attempt on a U.S. president.
1889 : The course of true love and Royal families has had

a history of tragedy that dates back to at least the nineteenth century. Austria's Crown Prince, Archduke RUDOLPH, and his 17-year-old mistress BARONESS MARIE VETSERA were found dead at the Royal hunting lodge of Mayerling. It was believed the couple died in a suicide pact. RUDOLPH was unhappy in his arranged marriage to STEPHANIE, daughter of the Belgian king. Another theory about the deaths was that the Prince was murdered because of his sympathies with Hungarian nationalism.
1933 : ADOLF HITLER was appointed Chancellor of Germany.
1937 : Thirteen leading Communists were sentenced to
death for allegedly participating in a plot, led by LEON TROTSKY, to overthrow the Soviet regime and assassinate its leaders.
1945 : The Duke of Gloucester became the first member of
the British Royal Family to be appointed Governor-General of Australia.
1948 : ORVILLE WRIGHT, one of the WRIGHT Brothers who
made the first powered flight, died.
1948 : MAHATMA GANDHI was assassinated in his own garden

in New Delhi, shot three times by NATHURAM GODSE. India's "Great Soul" was gunned down by a Hindu extremist who thought GANDHI's anti-partition policy was pro-Muslim and pro-Pakistan. GANDHI's last words were "Ram, Ram" meaning "Oh God, Oh God". The
assassin made no attempt to flee and had to be saved from the crowd by air force officers.
1958 : YVES SAINT LAURENT held his first major fashion
show in Paris at the age of 22, after spending four years studying under CHRISTIAN DIOR, who died in 1957.
1961 : The contraceptive pill went on sale in Britain for
the first time.

1968 : Viet Cong guerrillas and North Vietnamese
soldiers launched the Tet (New Year) offensive, targeting more than 100 towns and cities in South Vietnam. The offensive was militarily unsuccessful, but North Vietnam scored a psychological victory.
1965 : WINSTON CHURCHILL was buried. The British

conservative politician was Prime Minister twice once from 1940 to 45 and again in 1951 to 55. He began his political career in 1900 as a Liberal until 1923. He had earlier been a Boer war correspondent and had escaped from a Pretoria prison. He had a close relationship with US president ROOSEVELT and in February 1945 he met with the US president and Russia's JOSEPH STALIN to draw up the final plans for victory. On May 8 CHURCHILL announced the unconditional surrender of Germany. He resigned
1969 : The BEATLES staged their last "live" performance,
playing "GET BACK" on the roof of Apple Recording building in London.
1972 : British soldiers shot dead 13 people in a banned
Catholic civil rights march in Londonderry, Northern Ireland, in a clash known as "Bloody Sunday".
1973 : Watergate conspirators GORDON LIDDY and JAMES
McCORD were convicted of spying on the Democratic Party headquarters.
1983 : A mass African exodus began as Nigeria expelled
Ghanaians living within Nigerian borders.
1989 : Five black Pharaonic figures dating from 1470BC
were found in Luxor in Egypt.
1996 : HASAN MURATOVIC was formally appointed prime
minister of Bosnia Herzegovina's central government.
